summary: Glacier National Park's stone-based 1936 lookout above Swiftcurrent Lake, unstaffed from 1990 until a 2001 refurbishment restored service.

facts.design: 14x14 ft timber cab on a 10-foot stone base, flagstone-and-mortar roof, Swiss Chalet Revival detailing, no catwalk

access.note: reachable by trail in the Many Glacier area; active NPS lookout, not open for entry or rental

visit.trail_note: trail access, Many Glacier area, Glacier National Park

events.note: current stone-and-timber lookout built (one source gives 1935)
last staffed before a period of disuse
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 15, 1991

evidence.quote: Constructed in 1936, Swiftcurrent Lookout is one of the newest and most unique lookouts. The 14'x14'cab sits atop a 10-ft stone base. The gable roof is covered with a flagstone and mortar roof surface. A popular hiking destination, it is the only lookout in the Park without a catwalk.
The low two-story timber-construction structure with a gabled roof was built in 1936. Its detailing is reminiscent of the Swiss Chalet style of the nearby Many Glacier Hotel.

evidence.supports: built 1935 (per this source), last staffed 1990, refurbished, restaffed 2001
evidence.quote: Built in 1935, this stone and frame cab was last staffed in 1990. Refurbished, it was staffed again in 2001.

evidence.supports: design modified from standard USFS plans, part of a chain of lookouts
evidence.quote: The Swiftcurrent Fire Lookout in Glacier National Park is significant as one of a chain of staffed fire lookout posts within the park... The design is modified from standard U.S. Forest Service plans.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1935; NHLR and the Wikipedia/NRHP-derived text both give 1936. Noted as a discrepancy rather than resolved, since 1936 has two independent agreeing sources.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict (1935 vs 1936) and the 1990-2001 unstaffed gap are both worth flagging to an editor for a closer look at the NRHP PDF if available.
